children.value: > Fact From Story: In the complaint, Helena World Chronicle, which owns and publishes two weekly newspapers in Arkansas, argues that Google is “starving the free press” by sharing publishers’ content on Google, losing them “billions of dollars.”
> > Fact From Story: It also specifically cites new AI technologies like Google’s Search Generative Experience (SGE) and Bard AI chatbot as worsening the problem.
> > > Fact From Story: The suit points to Google’s older question-and-answer technologies, like the “Knowledge Graph” launched in May 2012, as part of the problem.
> > > Commonsense Knowledge: Older question-and-answer technologies can cause problems for news publishers.

> > Fact From Story: The case, filed by Arkansas-based publisher Helena World Chronicle, argues that Google “siphons off” news publishers’ content, their readers and ad revenue through anticompetitive means.
> > > Fact From Story: The U.S. lawsuit follows an agreement Google reached last month with the Canadian government which would see the search giant paying Canadian media for use of their content.

> > > Fact From Story: In addition to damages, the suit is asking for an injunction that would require Google to obtain consent from publishers to use their website data to train its general artificial intelligence products including Google’s own and those of rivals.
> > > Commonsense Knowledge: Lawsuits are often filed when one party believes another party has caused them significant harm.
> > Commonsense Knowledge: Taking content, readers, and revenue from news publishers harms their bottom line.
> Commonsense Knowledge: Losing billions of dollars would be harmful to a news publisher's bottom line.
